result.note: Tests the location of the offshore blocks, their area, minerals and deadline, and how this round relates to the failed 2024 round.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Ministry of Mines opened bidding for the Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01 offshore mineral blocks. In which sea are these blocks located?
questions.explain: The two blocks offered on 1 October 2026 lie in the Andaman Sea. An earlier offer of seven blocks near Great Nicobar in 2024 failed to attract sufficient qualifying bids.
questions.source: The Ministry of Mines opened bidding for two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea on Thursday, with submissions due by 28 December.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the offshore mineral blocks put up for bidding by the Ministry of Mines in October 2026:
items: The two blocks together cover more than 1,632 square kilometres.
According to the ministry, their seabed nodules and crusts contain cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements.
Bid submissions are due by 28 December 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements match the story. The ministry says these minerals are used in batteries, electronics and advanced manufacturing, and the bids cover both exploration and mining extraction rights.
questions.source: Mineral exploration and mining extraction rights over Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01, which cover more than 1,632 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Andaman Sea offshore mineral auction launched in October 2026:
items: The two blocks on offer are a re-auction of the blocks near Great Nicobar offered in 2024.
The launch announcement gives no estimate of how much mineral can be recovered or at what cost.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because a government official said the two blocks cover different areas and are not a re-auction of the seven blocks offered in 2024. Government surveys have established mineral occurrences in both areas, but India's domestic miners lack deep-sea experience, so success hinges on foreign partnerships.
questions.source: These two are different areas, rather than a re-auction, according to a government official.
